NO. 029 · Wetlands & Waterways / Ardeidae · Herons & Egrets

Intermediate Egret

中白鹭 · zhōng bái lù Ardea intermedia
Winter visitor Common 60–70 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

The hardest of the three white egrets

Between Little and Great Egret in size, with a yellow bill, black legs and yellow feet — nothing extreme, which is exactly why it is hard. One rule: if the gape stops short of the eye it is Intermediate; if it passes the eye it is Great.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • BillYellow, black in the breeding season, often with a dark tip; medium length — shorter than Great Egret's, longer and finer than Little's.
  • GapeThe gape line ends below the eye or just past its rear edge and does not extend conspicuously beyond the eye — the most reliable separation from Great Egret.
  • Legs & feetLegs black; feet yellow to black — between Little Egret (yellow feet) and Great Egret (all black).
  • SizeAbout 65 cm long; neck long but less extreme than Great Egret's; stands fairly upright.

Behaviour

Stands or walks slowly at the edge of shallow water, fish ponds and flats, taking fish, shrimp, frogs and aquatic insects. Usually alone or in small groups, mixing with Little and Great Egrets in winter. A winter visitor here from October to April at all kinds of wetland.

Voice

No openly licensed recording is available for this species.

A hoarse 'kraak', similar to Little Egret but slightly lower, given repeatedly when flushed.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Qi'ao Island tidal flats
  • Jinwan fish ponds
  • Doumen tidal creeks
  • Hengqin wetlands
Field note
Three egrets, fast: all-black bill with yellow feet is Little; a yellow bill with the gape stopping short of the eye is Intermediate; a yellow bill, gape past the eye and black legs is Great.
